name: Git for Global Law
cost: Free (CC0). The law text in each country's repo is under that repo's own terms.
works_with: Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code, Codex and any MCP client
short: The world's law as git history, so you can see any provision as it stood on any date and which law wrote each line.
what: Global Law puts each country's, state's or court's law in its own git repository, where every commit is one law taking effect. This repo gathers them as submodules and ships Python tools to show a provision on a date, list its changes, diff two dates and blame each line. It also has an MCP server and a free hosted connector.
who: Lawyers, researchers and developers who need to know what a law said on a given day. If you just want to look something up, the hosted search on the project's site needs no install.

steps.title: Clone the repo
steps.text: A shallow clone keeps it small.

steps.title: Add a body of law
steps.text: This adds the US Code. Swap in any other path from `manifest.json`.

steps.title: Read a provision on a date
Use it from your coding agent
steps.text: Opening the clone in Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code or Codex starts a local MCP server with the same tools. Hosted chat apps can use the free connector at `https://global-law.lexifina.com/mcp`.

try.label: From the README
try.text: Run `python3 tools/law.py log united-states/federal/usc/title-11/1182.md` to see every change to that section and the law that made it.

watch: Opening the clone in a coding agent starts a local MCP server on its own.
Coverage differs by country. Some publishers keep only today's text, and `manifest.json` says which.
Court decisions are added separately and the tools leave them out unless you name them.
